title: Basic English — Course 2, Semester 1 — Pilot Variant 15

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. When is the placement briefing?
tasks.audioText: The college placement coordinator will hold a briefing for students starting work experience next month. The meeting is on Thursday at ten in Lecture Room 5. Students should bring the contact details of their workplace supervisor and a copy of the placement agreement. The coordinator will explain attendance rules and how to report an absence.

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. Which document should students bring to the work-placement briefing?
tasks.audioText: The college placement coordinator will hold a briefing for students starting work experience next month. The meeting is on Thursday at ten in Lecture Room 5. Students should bring the contact details of their workplace supervisor and a copy of the placement agreement. The coordinator will explain attendance rules and how to report an absence.
options: A copy of the placement agreement

tasks.prompt: During her first week at a manufacturing company, Alina received instructions from her supervisor about recording completed tasks. She wrote down unfamiliar terms and asked for clarification when a step was not clear. At the end of each day, she checked her notes and prepared a short progress update. Her supervisor said that her reports were useful and easy to follow. Reading 1. What did Alina do when an instruction was unclear?
options: She repeated the instruction to the supervisor

tasks.prompt: What did she prepare at the end of each day?
options: A list of unfamiliar technical terms

tasks.prompt: The supervisor asked us ___ the completed checklist before leaving.
Choose TWO features of a useful workplace progress update.
options: A note about any problem that needs attention

tasks.prompt: A person who guides and checks a trainee's work is a ___.
You do not understand a workplace instruction. What should you say?
options: I will guess what to do.
Could you show me that step once more, please?

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of professional communication in a sensible order.
Write 60–80 words introducing yourself to a workplace supervisor. Mention your course, what you hope to learn and how you will communicate about your progress.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: the introduction identifies the course and what the student hopes to learn (0–2); it explains how progress will be communicated to the supervisor (0–2); the tone is professional and the message is organised with understandable grammar (0–2); workplace-learning vocabulary, spelling and punctuation are appropriate (0–2).
